Dry conditions are now expected for all the Marianas through Friday,
with the exception of island effect showers possible for all islands
Tuesday, as winds continue to weaken. These will likely remain 
shallow and short lived in nature due to dry air in the upper levels 
of the atmosphere. Some island effect is possible Monday but looks to
remain mostly offshore due to light northwest winds. By Friday night,
rainbands ahead of Invest 96W, currently north of Kosrae, may begin 
to move into the region and bring scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms. By Saturday night or sometime Sunday, heavier showers 
and thunderstorms will be possible along with gusty winds. However, 
the track and intensity of 96W is highly uncertain as the system has 
yet to organize and remains at least a week out. Residents in the 
Marianas should continue to monitor forecasts over the next several 
days, and maintain a general state of preparedness. See the "Tropical
Systems" section for more details on 96W.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 feet look to decrease through midweek to as low as
3 feet. Swells consist of a dominant north swell from distant Typhoon
Koguma and a smaller northeast swell. This will cause a moderate risk
of rip currents along north and east facing reefs through Monday night.
South and west facing reefs are now at low risk as any south or west
swell has become negligible. Seas are expected to increase sometime 
Friday ahead of Invest 96W. Light to gentle northwest winds will begin
to ease today and become light on Monday, becoming east to northeast
by early Wednesday and gradually increasing through the end of the 
forecast period.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Koguma (27W) has exited Guam's area to the north. 

Invest 95W is currently listed by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
(JTWC) as "Medium", meaning formation of a tropical cyclone (topical 
depression or stronger) is likely, but beyond 24 hours. It's located 
near 15.3N 150.1E, which is about 325 miles east-northeast of Saipan.
Slow strengthening and a gradual turn to the north, then northwest 
is expected over the next few days. It'll pass near Agrihan, 
possibly as a tropical depression, towards the middle of the week.

Then, the systems we've been receiving several calls on, is Invest
96W, located far from Guam to the southeast. It was upgraded from
"Sub-Low" to Low around 2:46 PM ChST by JTWC this afternoon. It's
current location is 9.8N, 163.1E, which is roughly 380 miles northeast
of Pohnpei, or about 1255 miles southeast of Andersen AFB, Guam. It 
continues to slowly organize, with better cyclonic flow. Convection 
has recently decreased, but that occurred as a circulation earlier 
this morning was located between Kwajalein and Wotje in the RMI 
(Republic of the Marshall Islands) merged with 96W, as discussed in 
the morning Tropical Weather Discussion. Thus, 96W is likely re- 
organizing, and we expect to see a reemergence of more robust 
convection during the next 24 to 36 hours.

The main questions on everybody's mind is where's it going, when will
it cross the Marianas, where, and at what strength. Unfortunately, 
we don't have all the answers yet, but here's what we're "moderately"
sure of...it'll arrive next weekend (give or take 12 to 24 hours). 
It'll pass somewhere between Guam and Pagan. It'll quite possibly be 
stronger than a tropical depression. THAT'S IT. In forecasting, the 
further out in time you go, the proverbial bigger the "haystack gets 
when trying to find the needle." Folks should continue to monitor our
social medial pages, and of course you can always call us, or check 
at www.weather.gov/gum

Eastern Micronesia...
Invest 96W was recently upgraded to "Low" by JTWC. It's currently
located near 9.8N 163.1E, or roughly 380 miles northeast of Pohnpei.
It's recently ingested a circulation that approached from the east 
(it was between Kwajalein and Wotje this morning), and is in the slow
organization process. We thought about hoisting a Special Weather 
Statement, but opted to wait until tomorrow to see if the earlier- 
anticipated ingest occurred, and what affects it would have on 
convection. As of right now, warmer, more shallow cloud tops have 
developed, but this could be short-lived as the two merging centers 
reorganize. This will likely foster renewed convective development 
over the next 12 to 36 hours. After which, it'll begin it's west- 
northwest journey.

At this time, Pohnpei and Kosrae look to see the "effects the most"
(especially Pohnpei), as a developing southwest inflow is expected by
48 hours. This should increase convective coverage and vigor, with
locally heavy rainfall likely developing at Pohnpei sometime between
